solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Meat, but no cake around American barbecue

indicators.note: 'no' says the letters of the following word are to be removed from the barbecue
'around' says the removed letters sit on either side of what remains, at the front and the back

parts.note: a clambake is an American seaside cookout of shellfish

explanation.surface: A diner at an American cookout who wants meat but skips dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'cake' are split: C comes off the front of CLAMBAKE and AKE off the back, so 'no cake around' leaves the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is the flesh of young sheep eaten as food, a familiar red meat.

clue.text: Girl first up, claiming female title

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the reversed word grips the title inside it
in a down clue 'up' says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lead is to be first, in front
Ms is a form of address for a woman

explanation.surface: A girl being first to get up and claim a woman's title, like a beauty queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old or literary word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Confusion surrounding mistake about appointment to view city flat?

indicators.note: surrounding says the confusion is wrapped round everything that follows

parts.note: pie is a printer's term for jumbled type, hence confusion

indicators.note: about means around, so the mistake is wrapped round the appointment

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
a date is an arranged appointment

explanation.surface: A muddle over a booking to view a flat in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusion' draws on printers' jargon: spilled, jumbled type is called pie. 'To view' only fills out the surface, and the question mark admits a pied-à-terre need not be a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small second home kept in a town for occasional stays, often an apartment.

clue.text: Turn down drink after a bit of dancing

indicators.note: 'after' places the drink behind the bit of dancing

parts.note: a pas is a step in ballet
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Declining a drink after a turn on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an offer is to decline or reject it, an idiom for refusing.

clue.text: Stop one making contribution to press leaf

parts.note: to end is to stop
paper is what goes into a printing press, and a newspaper is part of the press

explanation.surface: A journalist told to stop being a contributor to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpaper is the blank leaf pasted inside a book's cover and the flyleaf facing it.

clue.text: Program under test 50% improved? That's little advanced

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: improved means better
A is a little or abbreviated form of advanced

explanation.surface: A software tester judging whether a program is only half improved and barely advanced.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta version is software released for trial by users before final release.

clue.text: Japanese food? I try a koi, cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared differently, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sampling a carp at a Japanese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: A koi is an ornamental carp, though yakitori is in fact grilled chicken, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakitori is grilled chicken on skewers, a dish of Japan.

clue.text: Current point linked with dreadful films — insubstantiality

indicators.note: dreadful films are badly made ones, so the word is mangled into a new order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing poor films as having no substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsiness is the quality of being thin, weak or lacking substance.

clue.text: Antique instrument: one old woman recalled it

parts.note: a is one
ma is mother, an old woman in slang

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old woman remembering an antique instrument she once had.
explanation.definitionFit: Amati violins were made by a celebrated Cremona family of luthiers in the 1500s and 1600s.

clue.text: Hard to interrupt Allen in a funny film

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so the letter goes into the middle
funny means odd, so the letters are made strange by rearranging

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A hard-going interruption to a Woody Allen comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny film' reads as one phrase, but 'funny' rearranges ALLENINA into ANNIEALL, and H goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Hall is the 1977 Woody Allen comedy that won Best Picture.

clue.text: There's energy in the less important songs as well

indicators.note: in says one letter goes inside the songs

parts.note: B-sides are the secondary tracks on a single
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A fan noting there is real energy in a band's lesser tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides as an adverb means in addition, also.

clue.text: Good man is shifting money — a key skill

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good

indicators.note: shifting says one letter is moved to a new spot within the words

parts.note: M is short for money, as in economics

explanation.surface: A good man moving money around, as if banking were a key skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' hints at piano keys; M moves from the front of MANIS to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianism is the art and technique of playing the piano, an instrument of keys.

clue.text: Cracked line running through image

indicators.note: running through says the letter passes into the middle of the word

parts.note: spit as in spitting image, an exact likeness

explanation.surface: A crack showing as a line across a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as an adjective means broken apart along a line, cracked.

clue.text: University charity event kept up in depressions? Sweet things!

indicators.note: kept and in together say these pieces are held inside the downturns
in completes the containing signal begun by kept

parts.note: slumps are economic depressions

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' says the word is read upwards

parts.note: rag is a student fundraising event for charity in Britain

explanation.surface: Students' charity fundraising kept going through hard times, with a sweet treat at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is an annual British student charity drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar lumps are small cubes of sugar, sweet things in themselves and slang for darlings.

clue.text: Vigour shown by no salesman backing current meat product

parts.note: pep is energy, vigour

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these words are reversed

parts.note: taken as written
rep is short for sales representative
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A lively pitch that no salesman would back for a meat product.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried sausage, a cured meat product.

clue.text: Police ultimately unhappy about lively activity round traffic control feature

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so only the closing letter is used
about says the sad word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: sad means unhappy
a caper is a frolic or lively escapade
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Police unhappy about joyriding round a traffic feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape road is a run-off lane letting a vehicle that has lost control leave the road safely.

clue.text: Military man's exploit brought in cost in work for doctors

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

indicators.note: brought in says the exploit is placed inside the cost

parts.note: price means cost
an act is a deed or exploit

explanation.surface: A general's deed being costed by the army's medical staff.
explanation.definitionFit: General practice is family medicine, the work done by GPs in community surgeries.

clue.text: A short 'No'?

parts.note: split 3,1,4 the phrase describes a short person; read whole it is an emphatic no

explanation.surface: A curt negative reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Respaced as NOT A TALL, the answer describes someone short; as one phrase it is a firm refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Not at all is an emphatic negative, meaning in no way whatever.

clue.text: Erotic feeling about number one string player

indicators.note: about says the feeling goes around the number and one

parts.note: lust is sexual desire
ten is a number
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A desire stirred by the leading violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutenist plays the lute, a plucked stringed instrument.

clue.text: Turned back to be in Paris after end of October (unexpected date)

indicators.note: after puts the French verb behind that letter
end of says only the final letter of the month is taken

parts.note: etre is French for to be

indicators.note: unexpected signals a surprising new order for the letters

explanation.surface: A traveller who turned back from Paris in late October on a surprise date.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw or go back, so retreated means turned back.

clue.text: Change of direction? BBC chief suppresses curious expression

indicators.note: suppresses means holds down, so the chief's letters contain the look

parts.note: DG, Director-General, is the head of the BBC
an ogle is a leering, inquisitive look

explanation.surface: A BBC boss quashing an odd expression, marking a change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a sharp bend, as on a golf hole that turns partway along.

clue.text: City administrative district being trimmed

indicators.note: being trimmed says the district loses its tail letter

parts.note: a parish is a local administrative district in England

explanation.surface: A city borough being cut back in size.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France.

clue.text: Immediate response: 'Arbiter should be above law'

indicators.note: in a down clue being above means coming first

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an arbiter
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A slogan that the referee stands above the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an automatic, instant reaction.

clue.text: Transport to London put off after fall? On the contrary

indicators.note: after would place the anagram behind the fall
off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A trip to London postponed after a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: An up train is one heading towards London, the main terminus in British railway usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-train is British railway usage for a train travelling towards the capital.

clue.text: Soldier, if spurning force, is opposing force

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letter for force is cast out

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A soldier refusing force, a pacifist set against force.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as an adjective or preposition means against, in opposition.

clue.text: Animal's mistake about island and river

indicators.note: about says the blunder goes round the island and river

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: A wildlife slip involving an island and river.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is the tall long-necked African mammal.

clue.text: Test printing unit, importing Times article

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the unit takes the next letters inside

parts.note: an em is a unit of measure in printing
X is the multiplication sign, times
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A test for a print shop taking in copies of The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: European ensnaring one tragic heroine, showing gentility

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping, so the European holds the next pieces

parts.note: a Pole is a European
I is the Roman numeral one
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's tragic heroine

explanation.surface: A European trapping a doomed heroine with fine manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse is formal politeness or refinement of manner.

clue.text: Kipling character observed in lake repeatedly?

indicators.note: observed in says the answer is seen inside the doubled word, shedding its outer letters
repeatedly says the word is written twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spotting a Kipling figure in a lake, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 'lake' twice, LAKELAKE, and the character sits inside, minus the first L and the final KE.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the wolf pack leader in The Jungle Book, and the name of Cub Scout leaders.
